Notes: Editorial identification: Kalkoti pīlīl 'ant' belongs with CDIAL 8201 section 6 *pilīla-, comparing Palula pilī́lu and Gawri/Bashkarik pilíl. The pilīl- stem supports this branch rather than an undifferentiated link to pipīlá-. Inheritance is proposed; regional lexical exchange cannot be excluded. Imported vowel quantities are retained, not independently reconstructed.

Editorial identification: Kalkoti ic̣ [ɨʈʂ] 'bear' continues the ṛ́kṣa- family, comparing CDIAL Palula ĩc̣ and Shina forms and Degener's Shina ic̣ explicitly assigned to T. 2445. The i-vowel and retroflex affricate have close Shinaic parallels; Hultman documents coda deaspiration. No unattested Kalkoti accent or intermediate protoform is supplied.

Editorial extension of the existing Kalkoti aḍ/aṛ 'bone' assignment to the SSNP attestation ʔaḍ. Compare CDIAL Gawri/Bashkarik haḍ and Kashmiri aḍa; loss of h and weakening of the medial geminate fit the regional forms. The source's glottal onset is preserved. Turner explicitly regards a further connection with asthi-/aṣṭhi- as very doubtful, so no such link is proposed.

Hultman explicitly treats Kalkoti ìm as a loanword and compares Gawri him in the discussion of h-loss. Link as borrowed from the existing Gawri/Bashkarik him attestation (f_hwgei5m5eje26), already a reflex of CDIAL 14096 himá-, preserving that donor path. Hultman's low-tone mark is retained; it is not an assertion about Vedic accent.

Retain CDIAL 14064 as the provisional family index, not a claim of secure direct Indo-Aryan inheritance or a resolution of hā́rdi versus hr̥daya formation. Extend the accepted mætsin/məssin fish family to survey meʔʦīn / mesīn. Turner gives Gawri məts with plural -in; the survey spelling and number interpretation remain unchanged.

The parent is the encompassing entry, not specifically masculine ox.

Compare Palula āj, Sauji až and Gawri aj. Propose the same family for survey āž / āy; the second spelling may reflect a weakened consonant or survey transcription, without requiring a general ž > y rule.

Extend the already-linked Kalkoti khōr family to survey khor / khēr. The vowel contrast may be morphological, but the survey alone does not establish gender. Turner compares extended regional left-hand forms under kharva.

Compare the accepted Kalkoti buǰil family and Gawri bujj- 'hear', Palula bujj- 'understand'. The survey būy / būyīn can represent the same stem with a weakened palatal consonant. Keep the survey forms intact and treat the ending as modern morphology.

Compare Gawri ṭȫp 'hat' and the widespread ṭop/ṭopī family under *ṭōppa. Kalkoti ṭip is plausibly the local front-vowel form. The family is stronger than a specific vowel history; inheritance versus regional borrowing remains unresolved.

Propose gænarāṭ as an extended human noun based on gæn 'big', with the familiar big-to-elder semantic development also reflected in Turner's Gawri and Sauji comparanda under ghana. Hultman's example confirms old people and masculine plural agreement but does not analyze the word's internal morphology. The -arāṭ material remains unetymologized; this is a tentative derived link to the base, not inheritance of the whole noun.

Propose māś as the masculine counterpart of mēś 'mother’s sister', with back versus front vowel matching a recurrent regional gender pattern. The male and female referents are independently elicited in the same kinship source. A paired formation is more defensible than direct inheritance of the whole male term from mātuhṣvasṛ 'mother’s sister'; whether it arose within Kalkoti or was inherited as a pair remains open.

Tentatively analyze drəyīt as the feminine counterpart of drəvūt, with ū/ī and v/y differentiation. This would be a later paired formation within the already proposed brother-child family. Independent formation with a daughter-denoting second member remains an alternative, so a direct derivational sequence is not established. Keep the differently shaped drādi entry separate and unassigned.

CDIAL 9089 groups *phupphu-, *phupphī- and *phapphī- in one head and explicitly gives Shina phīpī/phīpi for father’s sister and mother’s brother’s wife. The modern phīpi and phapī series share this expressive kinship family. Rajapurohit’s final h, HKAT’s masculine-final phipō for uncle’s wife, and variable aspiration are retained as review points; the proposal does not pretend to select one uniquely recoverable proto-vowel from the grouped head. Rajapurohit also separately records phapī and phapyē for maternal uncle’s wife, the second relationship explicitly included in Turner’s Shina gloss; the latter ending is retained as an inflectional review point.

It is kept separate from the similarly shaped good adjective under śubha.

Same-page and numbered addenda do not alter this Shina comparison.

Degener’s primary glossary explicitly analyzes sam well as probably from sāma, referring to Turner 13346 and attributing the suggestion to Buddruss. The head record represents that grouped entry; no unexplained -ka reflex is asserted. The Backstrom/Schmidt good attestations and the well attestation share sam, but their grammatical gloss differences are preserved.

Propose a Shina nominal derivative of that attested verbal base, rather than treating the noun as a direct reflex of the Sanskrit finite verb guṇayati. The source relation and meaning support the analysis, while the precise history of the nominal ending remains to be checked. Degener also records gunanī th- think of; the current record is the noun alone.

Degener p. 251 explicitly identifies beyarij- be made to sit as the passive of the causative of bēi- sit. Degener p. 276 places kolij- become crooked, warp; remain silent, without answer beside kōlo crooked. Degener p. 302 explicitly derives šidalar- let cool down from šidálo cold and attests the absolutive šidalare. Degener explicitly glosses phacī little tail and identifies it as formed from phacō tail, marking the diminutive noun feminine against the masculine base. CDIAL 11241 vatsatara gives Shina bachar/basero and Bshk. bachēr, supporting the r-bearing calf family; retain the changed vowel pattern and diminutive sense rather than collapsing it into the distinct bachō calf entry under vatsa.
